paper_metadata.title: Effect of Nb Concentration on Thermal Stability and Glass-Forming Ability of Soft Magnetic (Fe,Co)-Gd-Nb-B Glassy Alloys

evidence.quote: Effect of Nb Concentration on Thermal Stability and Glass-Forming Ability of Soft Magnetic (Fe,Co)-Gd-Nb-B Glassy Alloys
Figures 2 and 3 show XRD patterns and DSC curves of the glassy alloy annealed for 600 seconds at temperatures ( Ta) ranging from 873 to 973 K

The alloy ingots were prepared by arc melting the mixtures of pure Fe, Co, Gd, Nb metals, and crystal B with purities of over 99.5 mass pct in an argon atmosphere. The alloy ingots were remelted 4 times to ensure chemical homogeneity.
The glassy alloy was produced by an injection copper mold casting for bulk cylindrical rods with diameters of 1 to 4 mm and by melt spinning for ribbons with a cross section of 0.02 9 1.0 mm2.
The alloy ingots were prepared by arc melting the mixtures of pure Fe, Co, Gd, Nb metals, and crystal B with purities of over 99.5 mass pct in an argon atmosphere.
The glassy alloy was produced by an injection copper mold casting for bulk cylindrical rods with diameters of 1 to 4 mm
The annealing sample was sealed in a quartz tube, evacuated to 1 9 10/C03 Pa, and then isothermally annealed for 600 seconds at temperatures ranging from 823 to 973 K by an annealing furnace.
The XRD patterns of the samples with diameters of 1.5 to 3 mm consist only of a broad peak, conﬁrming that a single glassy phase was formed.
The XRD and TEM results reveal that the initial crystalline phase for the (Fe0.9Co0.1)67.5Nb4Gd3.5B25 glassy alloy is a metastable (Fe,Co)23B6 phase.

the TEM image reveals some nanocrystalline particles with grain sizes of 10 to 30 nm in the glassy matrix (Figure 4(a)). The NBD patterns of the precipitation particles were identiﬁed to be a phase type of Fe23B6

mechanisms.name: glass transition stabilization by Nb addition

evidence.quote: The addition of Nb into (Fe,Co)-Gd-B alloy causes the sequent change in atomic sizes among the constituents ... and the generation of new strong chemical aﬃnities of Nb-B, Nb-Fe, and Nb-Co pairs, which contribute to the strengthening of the random networks of a trigonal prismlike local unit, leading to enhancement of the stabilization of the supercooled liquid.
a large positive heat of mixing between Nb and Gd (30 kJ/mol) could also contribute to repulsive chemical interactions, and may result in the local compositional ﬂuctuation in the supercooled liquid.

The precipitation of the Fe23C6-type phase having a complex fcc structure from the networklike glassy structure requires long-range atomic rearrangements of constituent elements and results in the enhancement of thermal stability of the glassy phase against crystallization, leading to the increase of GFA.
